  • The law of conservation of momentum states that the total momentum before the collision is equal to the total momentum after the collision. This is true regardless of the nature of the collision whether it is an elastic or an inelastic collision. 

  • Kinetic energy, on the other hand, is only conserved in elastic collisions. In these types of collisions, the objects bounce off each other without any loss of energy to heat, sound, or deformation.

  • In inelastic collisions, part of the kinetic energy is transformed into other forms of energy, such as internal energy (which might deform the objects), sound, or heat. Hence, kinetic energy is not conserved in inelastic collisions.
